team.ja: のんびりした生活シミュレーション（町で暮らし、住人と仲良くなるゲーム）を作っている小さなインディーチーム
team.en: a small indie team making a relaxed life sim (the player lives in a town and befriends its residents)

notes: Genre-level design questions a cozy / life-sim developer typically asks. Same fields as roguelite.json. The records hold no farming game yet (Stardew Valley and Harvest Moon / Story of Seasons are not on record), so questions that lean on farming expect a gap. The last question is a control with no matching reference. Re-check goldCases and expectGap whenever the playbook is regenerated, and update playbookCommit.

prompt.ja: ゲーム内の1日を現実の時計と同じにするか、ゲームの中だけの時計（1日20分など）にするか迷っている。現実の時計だと夜しか遊べない人が困りそう。
prompt.en: Should a day in our game follow the real clock, or a clock of its own (say 20 minutes per day)? With the real clock, people who can only play at night may miss out.

goldCases: Dobutsu no Mori / Animal Crossing (a village on the real clock; fish and bugs change with the hour; a father who plays at night can still catch a great fish)
Shenmue (every townsperson has a daily schedule the player reads to find them)
questions.expectGap: No farming-game developer on record explaining how long an in-game day lasts

prompt.ja: 1日に行動できる回数（体力）に上限を付けるべき？付けると『あれもこれもできない』とストレスになり、付けないと毎日が作業になりそう。
prompt.en: Should we cap how much the player can do in one day (an energy or stamina limit)? A cap may feel stressful, but without one each day may turn into a grind.

goldCases: Persona 3 (a school-year calendar with relationships on top)
Fire Emblem: Three Houses (time management as a selling point; an early strict limit on whom you can talk to was opposed)
Persona 4 (weather-driven deadlines made players rush dungeons and split them from relationships)
Persona 3 Reload (removed the condition system because it led to save-and-reload against the odds)
questions.expectGap: No farming or life-sim developer on record explaining a daily energy or stamina limit

prompt.ja: 住人との仲の良さを、ハートのゲージで見せるか、会話や態度だけで分かるようにするか。新しく引っ越してくる住人とも、ちゃんと仲良くなれる流れにしたい。
prompt.en: Should we show how close the player is to each resident as a heart gauge, or only through their dialogue and behaviour? We also want residents who move in later to become friends in a believable way.

goldCases: Persona 5 Royal (a new character everyone fawns over would feel unearned; bonds grow naturally, modelled on Marie in Persona 4 Golden)
Fire Emblem: Three Houses (meet most of the cast before the war so bonds exist when it matters)
questions.expectGap: No cozy-game developer on record explaining whether to show relationship values as a number or gauge

prompt.ja: 家族や友だちと一緒に遊べるようにしたいが、同時にオンラインで遊ぶのは予定を合わせるのが大変。どうすればいい？
prompt.en: We want families and friends to share the game, but getting everyone online at the same time is hard. What can we do?

goldCases: Dobutsu no Mori (up to four people live in one village but never at the same time; letters and a notice board pass messages)
Dobutsu no Mori (kept the shared field and built the game around players' communication)
Nintendogs (StreetPass brings the dog-park chats of owners passing each other)

prompt.ja: 毎日少しずつ遊んでもらいたい。ログインボーナスのような仕組みは嫌われそうだが、ほかにどんな方法がある？
prompt.en: We want people to play a little every day. Login bonuses feel cheap. What else works?

goldCases: Personal Trainer: Walking (hoarding steps was not enough motivation; a review of daily rhythm was)
Personal Trainer: Walking (hides the step count so checking at the end of the day is a small joy)
Club Penguin (free party items as proof of having been there)
Dobutsu no Mori (a real-clock village that ends each day with 'see you tomorrow')

prompt.ja: メインのストーリーを終えた後も、ずっと遊び続けられるようにすべき？それとも、きれいに終わらせたほうがいい？
prompt.en: After the main story ends, should the player be able to keep playing forever, or should the game end cleanly?

goldCases: Wilmot's Warehouse (ends after about six hours on purpose; an endless treadmill would be unethical)
Club Penguin (went the other way: run like a weekly activity magazine with new content)
questions.expectGap: No farming or life-sim developer on record explaining why their game has no ending

prompt.ja: 失敗やゲームオーバーを一切なくすつもりだが、それだと張り合いがなくて退屈になるのでは、と言われた。どう考えればいい？
prompt.en: We plan to have no failure or game over at all, but someone said it will be boring with nothing at stake. How should we think about it?

goldCases: Keep Talking and Nobody Explodes (dropped the serious bomb so it is tense but not scary)
Keep Talking and Nobody Explodes (kept inputs simple so a loss never feels like clumsiness; the difficulty is in the decisions)
questions.expectGap: No cozy or farming-game developer on record explaining a no-fail design or the pressure kept instead

prompt.ja: 最初のチュートリアルが長いとテストで言われた。説明を減らして自分で見つけてもらう形にしたいが、迷う人が出るのが心配。
prompt.en: Playtesters say our opening tutorial is too long. We'd like to explain less and let players discover things, but we worry some will get lost.

goldCases: The Witness (removed jumping and picking up so the puzzles teach without words)
Strange Horticulture (no tutorial, like opening a board game box; eye-catching animation to keep players from getting lost)
TUNIC (hints hidden as manual pages in the world, because full-screen tutorials can spoil surprises)
Rain World (started with no guidance; playtests forced a short line of text and a small guide creature)

prompt.ja: 町のお店の品物の値段は、季節や需要で変動させたほうがいい？
prompt.en: Should prices in the town's shops change with the season or demand?

questions.expectGap: Control question: the playbook has no case on shop price fluctuation; a good answer says there is no direct precedent instead of inventing one
